scope: Apple GPU NUMERIC_FAST; classical estimators only
execution_policy: Owner requested source programming only. No compilation, verification, tests, measurements or hooks were run.
common_quality_contract: No quality result is claimed. Preserve full data, precision, iterations, tolerances, randomness, refusal behavior and fitted-state lifetime. Qualify every reachable estimator with full-workload end-to-end A/B and independent task metrics before promotion.

affected_callers: other classical x_prep Gram stages using fast_sym_gram_into
entries.mechanism: Halve both existing Gram row partitions: 8192 to 4096 and 2048 to 1024. Existing tile-pair selection is unchanged. Workspace sizing and both Gram entry points consume the same chunk calculation.
entries.cost_reasoning: Shorter row chains create more independent threadgroups for all neighboring shapes; partial storage and fold work increase with the number of chunks.
entries.quality_scope: Centered sufficient statistics, coefficients, heldout regression/classification quality, selected regularization, Bayesian/ARD objectives, class covariance and ill-conditioned/large-offset inputs.
limitations: Only existing grid-Gram routes are affected; weighted Ridge/Bayesian routes that bypass this file do not change.
Keep existing Ridge/LARS/class covariance/Bayesian/ARD grid routes enabled in both arms; their *_OFF rollback defines must be absent.
All affected callers, including transitive consumers beyond the initial idea card, require future full-workload evidence.
No dimension dispatch rule was added or removed.

affected_callers: other classical x_prep Gram stages using fast_sym_gram_into
entries.mechanism: Fold chunk means, Gram entries and X-transpose-Y entries with four FP32 striped accumulators and a fixed pairwise finish instead of one dependent serial accumulator.
entries.cost_reasoning: Four independent accumulation chains can overlap loads/arithmetic; every chunk is retained and no new scratch is allocated.
entries.quality_scope: All L01 estimator quality gates plus cancellation, large offsets, near-constant columns, multi-output fits and class-masked covariances.
limitations: This changes FAST reduction order; no error or speed bound is claimed.
Inherited grid-Gram prerequisites are identical to L01 in both arms.
L01 plus L02 requires its own future combined A/B; independent decisions cannot establish the combined result.

entries.mechanism: Predict two held-out rows per thread at a time, reusing every path coefficient across the two complete ascending feature chains. Preserve the existing MSE block fold and every alpha/fold.
entries.cost_reasoning: Reuse path loads and expose independent prediction chains while consecutive threads still read corresponding contiguous row groups; register pressure rises.
entries.quality_scope: Selected alpha/l1 ratio, coefficients, dual gaps, heldout RMSE, fold isolation, path ties and final single-row tails.
limitations: Only the fast CV route is affected; its existing fold-layout eligibility and fallback remain unchanged.
The environment prerequisite is 1 in both arms, avoiding comparison with the separate team route.
This changes held-out prediction work grouping only, not residual updates during coordinate descent.

entries.mechanism: Use 256-row loss/gradient partials in the resident Huber solver instead of its default 512-row partials; scratch and witness launch counts follow the existing HF_FOLD-derived helpers.
entries.cost_reasoning: Shorten per-thread serial chains and expose more partial tasks, at the expense of scratch and final fold traffic.
entries.quality_scope: Robust objective, coefficients, scale, convergence status, outlier behavior, sample weights and heldout RMSE; tolerance and line-search budget unchanged.
limitations: Existing HUBER_DEVICE_LBFGS and default block512 routes must remain enabled in both arms.
This is a new 256-row schedule, not relabeling the already-default 512-row candidate.
No optimizer batching or stopping policy is changed.

affected_callers: LogisticRegression binary and multinomial QN paths
QN squared/absolute regression callers using the same gradient product
entries.mechanism: Use nominal 1024-row chunks and at most 512 gradient partials instead of 2048 rows and 256 partials. Workspace and launch planning share the new constants.
entries.cost_reasoning: Double available row parallelism while bounding scratch and final-fold work at twice the existing partial count.
entries.quality_scope: Logloss/accuracy or regression task metrics as appropriate, fitted coefficients, objective and optimizer status, class imbalance and extreme logits.
limitations: MOJOLEARN_QN_FAST_COALESCED_OFF is essential in BOTH arms because the default coalesced route otherwise bypasses this product.
Keep QN_FAST_XTDZ enabled in both arms; distributed gradient routes still bypass it.
Existing register-cell and class staging capacity limits remain unchanged.
The actual reach includes eligible single-output QN losses as well as the originally proposed multinomial case.

affected_callers: OneClassSVM through the same SMO fused update when applicable
entries.mechanism: Increase moved-row shared staging from 3072 to 4096 FP32 feature words. Kernel-row and alpha updates retain their complete ascending order.
entries.cost_reasoning: Amortize synchronization over a larger working-set row page. Including norm and delta pages, maximum shared storage is 24 KiB at KPAD=4, below Apple's 32 KiB floor.
entries.quality_scope: Margins, support vectors, solver convergence, regression residuals, anomaly ranking, SVR second-half updates and ragged moved-row tiles.
limitations: Limited to the inherited fused RBF/linear kernel update and its feature-register capacity; polynomial/sigmoid and wider feature routes do not change.
Keep MOJOLEARN_SVM_FUSED_UPDATE_F_OFF absent in both arms.
Narrowed from a possible new per-thread row microtile to a deeper supported moved-row staging schedule; working set and iteration budget are unchanged.

entries.mechanism: Partition the existing compensated centered covariance into nominal 2048-row partials, then compensate the partial fold and divide once by n-1. Means and input restoration contract are retained.
entries.cost_reasoning: Expose row parallelism in a one-chain-per-covariance-cell route. Partial scratch is limited to 16 MiB or one covariance matrix, whichever is larger, by reducing the number of row chunks.
entries.quality_scope: Explained variance, reconstruction, principal-subspace/orthogonality metrics, small singular directions, large offsets, rank deficiency and input immutability.
limitations: MOJOLEARN_PCA_FAST_COMPENSATED_COV must be enabled in BOTH arms; that older opt-in remains unpromoted.
This experiments on the compensated covariance route, not the default Apple matrix-unit covariance route.
Compensation is retained in both stages but a different association still needs downstream quality evidence.
Other PCA solvers and unrelated covariance consumers are not claimed to be covered.

affected_callers: other classical callers of x_decomp launch_gemm / DKit.mm
entries.mechanism: Increase the tiled product's K slab depth from 16 to 32, retaining the 32x32 output tile, 2x2 thread microtile, transpose handling and complete partial-K coverage.
entries.cost_reasoning: Halve slab synchronization frequency while growing the combined shared operand pages from 4 KiB to 8 KiB.
entries.quality_scope: Every affected estimator's full-operation task metrics plus product/solve/factor residuals, rank-deficient and ragged/transposed cases; no standalone GEMM admission.
limitations: MOJOLEARN_DECOMP_FAST_GEMM_TILED must be enabled in BOTH arms; comparison is against the older tiled schedule, not the default MMA route.
Only the classical x_decomp product entry changes; no global or neural GEMM dispatch was edited.
launch_gemm_ordered precision-sensitive callers bypass this candidate.
All transitive classical DKit.mm/DevExec.gemm callers need workload mapping before a default decision; the initial card's named estimators are not an exhaustive admission list.

affected_callers: randomized SVD when this QR route is selected
least squares when this QR route is selected
classical decomposition callers selecting the grid Householder route
entries.mechanism: Use 128-row reflector-product partials instead of 256-row partials; preserve the scaled norm reduction, signs, complete reflector sequence and existing finish/update kernels.
entries.cost_reasoning: Increase row-block parallelism and shorten dot-product dependency chains, with more partial scratch and fold work.
entries.quality_scope: Q orthogonality, QR/SVD reconstruction, least-squares residual, rank-deficient inputs and near-overflow/underflow scales.
limitations: MOJOLEARN_QR_FAST_DEV must be enabled in BOTH arms.
Implementation is explicitly the existing opt-in grid Householder QR route, not a change to blocked TSQR.
Callers that keep another QR route are unaffected and cannot be counted as measured coverage.

affected_callers: NMF solver=mu, beta_loss=frobenius; fit and transform
entries.mechanism: Specialize OP_MUZ dispatch and process four independent coalesced output stripes per thread using the existing ew_cell(OP_MUZ) arithmetic and broadcast indices.
entries.cost_reasoning: Reduce launched threadgroups and remove dynamic operation selection for a bandwidth-oriented update, while retaining zero-denominator replacement and FP32 operation order.
entries.quality_scope: Full reconstruction objective, nonnegative factors, stopping iteration, zero denominators, regularization, fixed-H transform and seeded initialization.
limitations: OP_MUZ was already a fused multiply/divide update; this is a new specialized work schedule and does not claim an additional eliminated intermediate.
Coordinate-descent NMF and non-Frobenius update formulas do not use OP_MUZ and are unaffected.
Four-cell grouping can reduce occupancy on small updates; no speed win is claimed.
L08 plus L10 requires separate whole-NMF combined evidence.

affected_callers: GaussianProcessClassifier binary/OVR latent variance and predictive probability
entries.mechanism: Use 128-query variance threadgroups in place of the default 256, preserving the complete ascending training-axis sum per query and all variance/std/clamp/probability work.
entries.cost_reasoning: Four SIMD groups per threadgroup expose more independently schedulable query groups without additional scratch or a query-count cap.
entries.quality_scope: Predictive variance/std, clamp placement, uncertainty calibration, probability logloss, ill-conditioned fits and query-batch invariance.
limitations: Only predictive-variance kernels change; GP fitting, cross-kernel formation, triangular solves and mean-only prediction are unaffected.
GPR's existing positive elem_tpb argument check remains, while the candidate intentionally chooses 128 for its production variance launch.
IDENTICAL segmented variance and sabotage launches retain their existing selection.
The source narrows batching to variance query tiles; it does not implement a new whole-prediction streaming workspace.

affected_callers: RBFSampler transform with a separate projection epilogue
RBFSampler resident fit_transform including its staged pipeline
entries.mechanism: Each thread applies the same random offset to one component in four consecutive rows; keep the same add/cos/multiply sequence, random draws and projected values.
entries.cost_reasoning: Reuse offset/index work over four rows while adjacent threads still access adjacent components; the final row group is explicitly tail-guarded.
entries.quality_scope: Feature-map error, seeded draws/offsets, downstream estimator quality, ragged row/component counts and resident/nonresident equivalence.
limitations: Only km_feature_map_epilogue callers are affected; already-fused projection/epilogue paths bypass the candidate.
Keep MOJOLEARN_RBF_FUSED absent in both arms when evaluating the nonresident separate-epilogue path.
Nystroem and KernelRidge were ideas in the broad card but are not reached by this cosine epilogue and are not claimed as implemented coverage.
The production code resides under checks/random_features.mojo; no test or check was executed.

entries.mechanism: Select each C-step trial's support with 128 threads rather than 256; all eight radix passes and the ascending-index tie scan remain. Initial and iterative support selection use the same geometry.
entries.cost_reasoning: Private histogram and scan shared storage falls from 17.125 KiB to 8.625 KiB per trial, permitting more concurrently resident trial groups at the cost of more rows per thread.
entries.quality_scope: Robust covariance, location, precision, support/tie membership, anomaly ranking, contamination behavior, singular trials and convergence.
limitations: Use the accepted default MCD_BATCH_MMA/BMMA route in both arms; no legacy rejected covariance route is enabled by this card.
The candidate only changes support selection grouping, not covariance arithmetic, eigensolves, random starts, C-step limits, support size or reweighting.
Existing route capacity limits and fallbacks remain unchanged; callers bypassing mcd_fast do not establish coverage.
Earlier active-compaction and covariance-reuse experiments stay separate and off during isolated A/B.

affected_callers: Perceptron/PassiveAggressiveClassifier/PassiveAggressiveRegressor when using the separate minibatch row kernel
SGDOneClassSVM when using the separate minibatch row kernel
entries.mechanism: Schedule independent minibatch prediction/loss rows in 128-thread blocks instead of 256-thread blocks; witness capacity, offsets and launch count use the same new row-grid helper.
entries.cost_reasoning: Expose twice as many independently schedulable row blocks while retaining each row's complete predictor, unchanged batch membership and all gradient/update passes.
entries.quality_scope: Heldout loss/accuracy/RMSE, seeded shuffle and class/sample weights, learning-rate progression, convergence, objective, one-class intercept and final partial batches.
limitations: The supported implementation lives in x_linear rather than glm; it is the actual classical SGD minibatch route.
Single-block chunked minibatches and per-sample SGD bypass this row kernel; do not claim those settings as affected coverage.
No batch size, epoch count, ordering, learning-rate policy or gradient-fold order is changed.
Dense device row kernels are covered; sparse input routes are not newly implemented.
The IDENTICAL-only fused step/row schedule retains the original geometry because this control requires NUMERIC_FAST.
